source_title: 7 things to know about the 2027 KTM 200 Duke - Autocar India
source_excerpt:
KTM has just given another update to the 200 Duke making it two in the same year. In early 2026, the sport-naked gained a new colour option, larger front disc and lighter alloy wheels. So, what else has it changed now? Let’s see.
Are there any changes to the engine and chassis on the KTM 200 Duke?
No, there aren’t. The motorcycle retains the 199.5cc, single-cylinder unit making 25hp at 10,000rpm and 19.3Nm at 8,000rpm. The 6-speed gearbox remains unchanged as well, save for the addition of the bi-directional quickshifter.
Chassis remains unchanged too with the bike retaining its tubular trellis frame with a bolt-on subframe. The 200 is suspended by a WP Apex made 43mm USD fork at the front and the preload adjustable monoshock at the rear.
There are four colours in total, two of which are new. Liquid Carbon and Slate Grey are new additions to the pre-existing Dark Galvano and Electronic Orange. Of course, this means the Atlantic Blue colour (launched earlier this year) has now been discontinued. Besides the colours there are no other differences between them, and they all cost the same.
That’s where the 200 Duke has been upgraded massively. With the recent update, the 200 Duke has gained a ride-by-wire throttle, two ride modes (Rain and Street), a bi-directional quickshifter, traction control and a crawl assist feature to help with stop-and-go traffic. Earlier this year, KTM added lighter alloy wheels and a 20mm larger 320mm front disc, both of which first debuted on the Gen 3 390 Duke ; the rear disc remains 230mm and dual-channel ABS is standard. In 2024, KTM upgraded its LCD screen to a 5-inch TFT unit from the Gen 3 250/390 Duke.
As things stand, the 200 Duke actually offers two extra features not on the bigger 250 Duke, which are traction control and ride modes.
What do I gain by paying Rs 19,000 extra for the 250 Duke?
You gain 6hp and 5.7Nm, which should make a noticeable difference on highway runs. The 250 Duke also gets the latest Gen 3 design language, whereas the 200 is still sticking to a Gen 2 design that’s now six years old.
However, you lose two features by going to the 250 as mentioned earlier, ride modes and traction control. KTM is yet to clarify when the bigger brother is expected to get it.
Does the 200 Duke also get cruise control?
No, it does not. If you’re looking for a KTM sport-naked with cruise control functionality, your only option is the 390 Duke (or the 390 Duke R ).
Why is the 200 Duke so expensive compared to other 200s?
Since its launch, KTM has positioned the 200 at the premium end of the market and that has not changed with time. The latest version is looking to justify that premium with its updated set of electronics and the brand’s famous reputation for sporty handling and performance. However, it’s no longer the most expensive 200 on the market. That title is now held by the new Yamaha R2 , which starts at Rs 2.30 lakh and tops out at Rs 2.53 lakh.
What’s the price of the updated KTM 200 Duke?
For the comprehensive set of new features, KTM has increased the 200 Duke’s prices by Rs 1,554 than before, taking the ex-showroom price to Rs 2.07 lakh. Above the 200 sits the 250 Duke, at Rs 2.26 lakh and below sits the 160 Duke TFT version at Rs 1.91 lakh.
